Challenging DOM

The hardest part in automated web testing is finding the best locators (e.g., ones that well named, unique, and unlikely to change). It's more often than not that the application you're testing was not built with this concept in mind. This example demonstrates that with unique IDs, a table with no helpful locators, and a canvas element.

text:
I found the row, read the Diceret cell, and clicked its edit link.

- **Diceret cell value:** `Phaedrum4`
- **URL after the click:** `https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/challenging_dom#edit`. The edit link only added the `#edit` fragment. The page didn't navigate anywhere else, and the table looked the same afterward.

**Evidence used to identify the row:**
- The page text and the screenshot both showed one row whose first cell (the Lorem column) read "Iuvaret4". It was the fifth data row, between Iuvaret3 and Iuvaret5.
- The Diceret column is the sixth column in the header. In the Iuvaret4 row, that cell read "Phaedrum4". The rest of the row read Apeirian4, Adipisci4, Definiebas4 and Consequuntur4.
- I clicked the "edit" link in the Action column of that same row, at the same height as the Iuvaret4 text. After the click, that link showed a focus or hover highlight.
